source.title: Clique topology reveals intrinsic geometric structure in neural correlations.
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

confidence_rationale: Rat hippocampal pyramidal-cell recordings analysed with an explicitly higher-order method (cliques are simplices; Betti curves are homology of the clique complex), finding structure that eigenvalue-based pairwise analysis misses. That is close to a direct demonstration that higher-order relational structure is present and informative in hippocampal population activity. Held below 0.8 because the higher-order object here is an ANALYST'S projection over a pairwise correlation matrix, not a demonstration that the circuit represents or uses hyperedges -- which is exactly Q-084's organisational-versus-representational distinction.
failure_signatures: Standard eigenvalue/PCA analyses of the same correlation matrices fail to distinguish geometric from random structure in the presence of unknown monotone nonlinearities, so a pairwise-summary readout can be actively misleading rather than merely incomplete.

Geometric organisation of correlations persists during wheel running and REM sleep, i.e. when there is no spatial position to code, so the structure cannot be explained as a downstream consequence of position coding -- an REE analogue would be topological structure in anchor correlations that survives removal of the spatial payload.

The clique-topology signal is computed from a PAIRWISE correlation matrix; a positive result therefore does not establish that anything above a pairwise relation is stored, only that the pairwise relations have higher-order geometric consequences.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Applying clique topology (Betti curves of the order complex, invariant under monotone nonlinear transformations of matrix entries) to rat hippocampal pyramidal-cell correlations detects geometric organisation that eigenvalue-based methods cannot, and the same geometric signature appears during non-spatial behaviours including wheel running and REM sleep.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-084 asks whether higher-order relational structure -- metapaths, hyperedges, simplicial relations -- is required, given that nothing in the REE registry represents anything above a pairwise relation. This paper supplies the strongest form of the affirmative available in the biology: a higher-order (simplicial) READOUT over hippocampal population structure extracts organisation that pairwise-summary methods provably miss. For REE that is a direct argument for the MECH-468/Q-084 comparison being worth running -- a metapath-aware readout may see what a typed-pairwise projection does not -- and a warning that a null from a pairwise-summary readout is weak evidence of absence.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The decisive caveat is the one Q-084's own notes insist on: this is an ORGANISATIONAL result obtained with a higher-order ANALYSIS METHOD applied to pairwise data, not evidence that the hippocampus represents hyperedges or that REE should be reimplemented as a hypergraph or simplicial complex. The paper's higher-order object lives in the analyst's toolkit. Additionally this is rat electrophysiology over anatomical position correlations; REE's anchors are action-object and trajectory structures with no guarantee that their correlation geometry behaves comparably, and the paper says nothing about metapaths of TYPED edges, which is Q-084's specific formulation.
mapping.source_context: Rat hippocampus, pyramidal-cell population recordings during 2D open-field exploration, wheel running, and REM sleep; topological data analysis of correlation matrices plus simulation controls.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (PNAS, strong method paper with simulation controls, well replicated as a technique). Mapping fidelity moderate: it supports the ORGANISATIONAL half of Q-084 and is silent-to-negative on the representational half. Transfer risk elevated -- rodent spatial ephys to REE action-object anchors is a long jump, and 'higher-order analysis of pairwise data' is not 'higher-order representation'.
